evidence:
Authoritative frozen workbook inspected with openpyxl: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks row 29 (check 28), says 'No two criteria grade the same thing twice, subsume each other, or demand incompatible products.' Internal Quality Checks row 29 has the historical whole-flow annotation; it is interpretation, not an override. Frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:120-121 permits flow bundling, but current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 explicitly supersedes a blanket bundling exemption: 'Share their browser scenario while scoring distinct promises separately. Preserve valid observations rather than inheriting a sibling verdict.'

Scope: inspected all 73 criterion blocks (58 Functional, 7 Polish, 6 Visual, 2 gates), all five judge prompts, app_context, and all six public notes. The main current ownership boundaries are substantially improved: functional/prompt.md:98-113 forbids inherited verdicts and repeated scenarios; S02 provides lowercase and JS-created CSS controls (:143-149); S22 separates retained durable reads from continued writes (:363-369); S23 separates server refusal from dirty-editor behavior; visual/prompt.md:17-22 expressly reserves mobile clipping/operability to Polish and Functional theme changes to Functional. Error message, exact line and restored preview are separately scored. No incompatible-product pair was demonstrated. Static restored previews versus interactive currently successful previews are compatible under behaviour.md:11-15 and app_context.md:18; optional provisional display, native keyboard controls, and mobile drawers/stacking likewise conform.

Confirmed source-level defect: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:183 makes cw_js_error_rollback require 'the JS failure restores B, not A or failed-partial-dom; an ordinary recovery Run works.' The same extra conjunct appears for cw_html_error_rollback at :204, cw_timer_error_rollback at :225 and cw_promise_error_rollback at :246. Corresponding public behavior distinguishes restoration of the already successful render (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:13,15) from later ability to run it again (:13; policy.md:5). The prior successful preview and exact failed/last-good render comparison already establish the positive control and direct restoration observation. A later new Run is a distinct operation, not evidence necessary to determine which render was restored. Combining those two useful promises in each binary row erases the observed restoration result if later execution is broken; the converse also loses all recovery credit when only rollback is broken. This is the same separation that S22 explicitly preserves for durable readbacks versus later writes (judge.toml:351,358; prompt.md:367-369). The general instruction to score rows independently cannot rescue two conjuncts inside one binary row.

The four implicated weights are 0.90, 0.50, 0.50 and 0.50: 2.40 out of the parsed Functional total of 32.70 (58 rows), representing 0.0440 of final shaped reward above the common floor. This quantifies affected scoring mass, not a measured model reward or the exact amount an eventual reweighting would restore.

Raw evidence was checked directly, without consulting other reviews. qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json matches the frozen Functional judge and prompt SHA256 values (8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d and 6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1). Its facts.S10.js_error_rollback.evidence has last_good.body='latest-good-B', restored='latest-good-B', recovered=true. S11, S12 and S13 likewise record respectively restored='js-error-recovered', 'html-error-recovered', and 'timer-error-recovered', each with recovered=true. Thus the actual observations distinguish restoration from subsequent execution. The executed drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:95-104 implements the same conjunction at :104: failed.body===lastGood.body && !failed.body.includes(c.candidate) && recovered. drivers/run_workflow.cjs:5,38,50 routes S10-S13 to that driver. These golden observations show the complete app satisfies both promises; they do not refute the partial-implementation counterexample. No deficient-app browser run, configured judge result, Oracle grade or target-model score was produced by this review.
counterexample: Plausible partial implementation, reasoned from the explicit binary descriptors and not claimed as an executed mutation: the error handler correctly replaces the failed iframe with its saved lastGood document and reports the error/line, but leaves the Run button disabled because the exception path fails to clear a running/busy flag. In S10, successful A and distinct B establish real controls; the four-line bad.js fixture restores exactly latest-good-B. The next ordinary js-error-recovered Run cannot start. cw_js_error_rollback must receive 0 despite directly proven correct rollback, solely because of the distinct later execution failure. The same implementation defect affects the HTML, timer and Promise exception paths. Conversely, an app can clear the preview after failure yet accept the recovery Run; its recovery promise also has no independent credit in these four rows. A fully conforming alternative that restores a static snapshot (no live handlers) and then accepts Run is explicitly allowed and was not flagged; I also checked that a dead/no-op runner cannot earn these restoration outcomes from absence because the protocols require an actual prior successful DOM/log control. No separate credible duplicate-observable or incompatible-product witness was established.
suggested_fix: Keep each existing S10-S13 browser scenario, successful controls and later recovery action, but assign restored-preview evidence and post-error successful-Run evidence to separate binary outcome owners; redistribute the existing criterion weight rather than adding duplicate setup or changing shared budgets/reward policy, and preserve one outcome when the other fails.
